get.summary: List or search the cards
get.description: Cards read in creation order, oldest first, so a walk never skips a card that moves between columns. `q` narrows the walk and does not rank it. Terminal columns are included.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project id or a project slug. A slug changes when the project is renamed, so quote the id when it must stay valid.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most rows to return.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The opaque position from the `next` URL of the last page.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The walk order. A leading `-` is descending. `createdAt` is the same order as `number`, because a number counts up in creation order.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search words, in the title and the body of every card. Matching is by substring, ignoring case. Every word must match. Quote a phrase, prefix `-` to exclude, and write `or` for either. `12` or `#12` also finds that card.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only cards in the column with this slug.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only cards of this type key.

parameters.name: reporter
parameters.description: Only cards raised by this reporter.

parameters.name: parentCardId
parameters.description: Only the children of the card with this id.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Only the children of the card with this number. Do not pass it with `parentCardId`.

parameters.name: paused
parameters.description: True for only the cards with an active pause, and false for only those with none.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only cards whose state is of this kind. A card shows one state, the first of its reasons, and this filter reads that one. A card in a terminal column has no state, so `status=done&state=working` answers an empty list. A card that enters or leaves the state during a walk can be missed, as with `status` and `paused`. One kind per request.

parameters.name: stateCode
parameters.description: Only cards whose state has this code, such as `run-open` for a running worker. The codes belong to the workflow of the project, so a code that no state has answers an empty list. Pass it with `state` to narrow a kind.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: The fields to return, as a comma list such as `number,title`. Each named field comes back whole, and nothing else does. `all` returns the whole resource and stands alone.

delete.summary: Lift the workflow pause of a card
delete.description: The workflow pauses a card when a rule used up its retries or its work limit, or when a worker stopped with a refusal that the workflow does not retry. Lift a pause only when its cause is gone. A pause of kind `rule` ends only on its own release condition. This call differs from the hold route, which makes a card unmanaged.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project id or a project slug. A slug changes when the project is renamed, so quote the id when it must stay valid.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The card number, the short label that counts from 1 inside this project.

parameters.name: pauseId
parameters.description: Lift this pause only, so a pause that changed since you read it is refused. Leave it out to lift the active pause.

put.description: Backlog always comes first and never moves, so leave it out. `errors[].code` is `backlog_in_order`, `unknown_column` or `order_incomplete`.

put.summary: Leave a card out of an experiment
put.description: The comparison then drops the card from every figure, metric, control and headline of every variant, and lists it with the left-out reason `excluded`. A second call replaces the reason, the author and the time. The experiment must list the card, and a listed card with no number cannot be reached. `DELETE` on the same path puts the card back.

delete.summary: Put a card back into an experiment
delete.description: Clears the manual exclusion of the card. The card counts again, unless an automatic left-out reason still applies to it. A card with no exclusion is left as it is, and the call still succeeds.

get.description: The cards that the Cards tab of the experiment lists, the latest run first and the cards with no run last. Each card names its variant, its pull request URLs, why the comparison leaves it out, and its manual exclusion. The state of the experiment can change between two pages of a walk, so a card can repeat or be missed.

post.summary: Put an item in the inbox of the owner
post.description: Hands one question, to-do or notice to the owner of the project, who answers it in the Loupe inbox. Nothing waits on the item, so `blocking` is always false, and the owner can dismiss any item. With `dedupeKey`, a call returns the open item that holds the same key with 200 and creates nothing. `Location` names the item. Read the answer with `getInboxItem`. The item names the API key that made it.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project id or a project slug. A slug changes when the project is renamed, so quote the id when it must stay valid.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key of your choice. A retry with the same key and body answers as the first request did. The same key with another body gets 409 `idempotency_key_reused`.

200.description: The open item that already holds the `dedupeKey`. Nothing was created.

get.summary: Read one inbox item and its answer
get.description: Returns the item with the answer of the owner, the same fields as the `inbox_get` MCP tool. `selectedOptions` holds the indexes of the options the owner picked, and `note` holds the words of whoever closed the item. `apiKey` names the key that made an `api-key` item.

parameters.description: A project id or a project slug. A slug changes when the project is renamed, so quote the id when it must stay valid.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: The item id, as `createInboxItem` returns it.

post.description: Loupe adds a tooling card to Backlog, and a bridge that serves the project runs a read-only worker on it. The worker checks the repository and the workflow, and writes a readiness report that lists what remains and who acts. The request takes no body. `url` is the Workshop page of the project, whose discovery row opens the report once the worker has written it. `Location` names the card. A live bridge must serve the project, the project must have a workflow with board automation on, and only one run can be open at a time.
